title: God Can Renew You and Your Relationships (Ephesians 4)
metaDescription: Feel totaled by sin, anxiety, or a broken relationship? In Ephesians 4:17-32, Paul shows how God renews us from the inside out and heals our relationships.
bodyHtml:
Picture a car that has been in a serious wreck. The frame is bent, the glass is shattered, the damage runs so deep that the insurance company doesn't repair it — they tow it and call it totaled. Beyond repair. Not worth fixing.

Maybe that word describes how you feel right now. Some of us feel totaled personally — by crippling anxiety, by a depression that won't lift, by a sin that keeps dragging us back no matter how hard we try. Others feel totaled relationally — a marriage, a friendship, an in-law, a coworker, and the relationship feels beyond repair. If that's you, here is the good news from this week's message: there is a God, and His name is Jesus Christ, and He specializes in renewing broken individuals and broken relationships.

This message continues our Grace for You series, our verse-by-verse walk through Ephesians. We're in Ephesians 4:17-32, and the main idea is simple and hopeful: God can renew you, and God can renew your relationships.

God Can Renew You

Paul begins by reminding believers of the life they left behind: "Now this I say and testify in the Lord, that you must no longer walk as the Gentiles do, in the futility of their minds. They are darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, due to their hardness of heart" (Ephesians 4:17-18).

Notice the phrase "no longer." Every saint has a past, and every sinner has a future. But the pull of the old life is real. We drift back to the very things God rescued us from — like knowing a certain food will make you sick and eating it anyway. The point is this: what we do comes from within. Sin isn't mainly a reaction to what's around us; it grows from a hardened heart and a darkened mind. Big sins rarely appear out of nowhere. We fantasize, we rehearse, we think about it — and darkened thinking leads to darkened living.

So real change isn't about dressing up the outside. It's transformation from within: "Put off your old self... and be renewed in the spirit of your minds, and put on the new self, created after the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness" (Ephesians 4:22-24). Two steps stand out:

  • Exchange the lie for the truth. Sin lies to us by advertising the momentary pleasure and hiding the long-term damage. It over-promises and under-delivers. Jesus, however, says, "I came that they may have life and have it abundantly." His commands don't restrict you; they free you.
  • Change the way you think. "Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth" (Colossians 3:2). You are not a helpless victim of your thoughts. Are you a thermometer, just reflecting the temperature of the world around you — or a thermostat, setting your mind by the Spirit? "To set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace" (Romans 8:6).

A practical starting place: read a little Scripture to begin and end your day, and pick one verse to memorize and meditate on. When you have empty moments, think deeply on that verse instead of doom-scrolling. As your mind is shaped by Scripture, your life will follow.

Speak Truthfully and Constructively

Once God renews you, He wants to renew your relationships — and that starts with your words. "Therefore, having put away falsehood, let each one of you speak the truth with his neighbor, for we are members one of another" (Ephesians 4:25). Lying breaks trust faster than almost anything. The short-term pain of telling the truth is far better than the long-term pain of losing a relationship built on a lie.

But truth must be delivered constructively: "Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up, as fits the occasion, that it may give grace to those who hear" (Ephesians 4:29). Before you speak, ask: "Is what I'm about to say going to build this person up?" Sometimes building up means gently naming a problem that needs to be addressed — and sometimes it means the right words spoken at the right time. The right thing said at the wrong time can become the wrong thing. A simple rhythm helps: pause, pray, then say. When we tear others down, we "grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption" (Ephesians 4:30).

Choose Forgiveness Over Bitterness

"Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger, and give no opportunity to the devil... Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and slander be put away from you, along with all malice. Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you" (Ephesians 4:26-27, 31-32).

Three things stand out here. First, godly anger is not bitterness — there is a way to be angry without sin, the way Jesus was angry when His Father's house was misused. Second, don't let anger harden into bitterness. Bitterness is frozen anger. It builds slowly, offense by offense, like plaque clogging an artery, until it damages both the relationship and your own heart. As the saying goes, bitterness is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die.

Third, God's forgiveness empowers our forgiveness. We forgive others as God in Christ forgave us — freely, fully, and forever. When Peter asked how often he must forgive, Jesus answered, "I do not say to you seven times, but seventy-seven times" (Matthew 18:22). We put limits on grace; God does not. And a chronically unforgiving heart reveals a heart that has never truly grasped how much it has been forgiven.

Stephen, the first martyr, prayed for the very people stoning him — echoing Jesus from the cross. In that crowd stood a man named Saul, who would become Paul, the author of Ephesians and the greatest messenger of God's forgiveness in history. That is what forgiveness unleashes.

Your Takeaway

Ask yourself honestly: In what way do you need God to renew you? Which relationship needs His healing? Is there bitterness you've been carrying past sundown for years? God never turns away anyone who comes to Him asking for renewal. If you're ready, you can pray right now: "Lord Jesus, renew me from the inside out. Forgive me, and help me extend that same forgiveness to the people in my life."

If this message encouraged you, we'd love to worship alongside you. If you're anywhere in Livermore or the Tri-Valley, come as you are — we'd be honored to have you join our church family this Sunday.
